key_insight: A three-stage framework plus MoTok—a diffusion-based discrete motion tokenizer—bridges semantic discrete planning and continuous diffusion control, enabling interpretable token-level conditioning while preserving high-fidelity kinematic synthesis.
problem_solved: Existing motion generation approaches trade off between semantic control (discrete token models) and kinematic fidelity (continuous diffusion models); this work unifies both so models can use discrete semantic conditions without losing realistic continuous motion.
method: Perception: extract compact semantic and kinematic condition features from inputs (e.g., text, labels, sensor signals).
Planning: generate discrete motion tokens using MoTok, a diffusion-trained tokenizer that captures a tokenized motion prior aligning semantics with motion structure.
Control: condition a continuous diffusion-based motion synthesizer on the generated tokens to produce high-fidelity, kinematically-plausible trajectories.
impact: Enables AI/ML practitioners to combine interpretable, discrete planning with state-of-the-art continuous motion synthesis—improving controllability and realism for animation, virtual characters, and robotic motion tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the three stages: Perception → Planning (MoTok) → Control, with arrows indicating flow from semantic inputs to continuous motion output.
Side-by-side comparison: discrete token sequence (icons/blocks) vs. resulting continuous trajectory (smooth curve/pose frames) to illustrate token-to-motion mapping.

Qualitative results panel: example motions conditioned by the same semantic prompt for baseline discrete, baseline diffusion, and the proposed hybrid—highlighting semantic accuracy and kinematic quality.
Schematic of the diffusion-based tokenizer: noisy token trajectories → reverse diffusion denoising → discrete token outputs, showing how MoTok learns token priors.
paper_title: Bridging Semantic and Kinematic Conditions with Diffusion-based Discrete Motion Tokenizer
paper_authors: Chenyang Gu, Mingyuan Zhang, Haozhe Xie, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang
